This page documents how a PAGe holdout cycle is built and audited. It is the
operational diagram for the exchangeable-season protocol: choose one untouched
holdout label, run complete leave-one-season-out (LOSO) tuning inside each
stage using the remaining training seasons, freeze the stages in order, and
only then replay the holdout.

::: {.callout-important}
## Core rule

The holdout season is never a tuning fold. It is not used to select a grid,
fit a final stage, choose a boundary expansion, or create M1 labels. The
holdout is opened only after the M0, M1, and M2 artifacts have passed their
stage gates and have been assembled into a validated kit.
:::

## Season sets and notation

For a selected holdout season $H$, define:

- $S$ as the eligible, exchangeable seasons in the data contract;
- $E$ as permanent exclusions (currently `2011-12`, `2020-21`, and
  `2021-22`; `2015-16` is treated as a special ignition/drop-test cycle);
- $T_H = S \setminus (E \cup \{H\})$ as the training seasons for this cycle;
- $F \in T_H$ as one LOSO evaluation fold; and
- $T_{H,F} = T_H \setminus \{F\}$ as the fold's actual fitting seasons.

The label of a season is only an identifier. It is not a chronological rule:
when `2024-25` is held out, `2025-26` may be a member of $T_H$ if the chosen
development cycle declares it eligible. The season-selection object records
this decision explicitly and rejects overlaps.

For every stage, the full LOSO score is the collection

$$
  \{\operatorname{score}(\theta, F; T_{H,F}) : F \in T_H\},
$$

not a score from one global fit. A candidate is selected only after every
required fold is complete and finite.

## End-to-end holdout diagram

The same structure is used for every holdout. The inner loops are shown
explicitly because they are the part most easily mistaken for a single global
fit.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["Choose holdout H"] --> B["Declare T_H, exclusions, and H\nvalidate_season_selection()"]
    B --> C

    subgraph M0["M0: ignition — complete LOSO"]
      C["For each fold F in T_H"] --> C1["Fit/tune M0 on T_H minus F"]
      C1 --> C2["Run ignition prospectively on F"]
      C2 --> C3["Record fold loss and boundary report"]
      C3 --> C
      C3 --> C4["Aggregate all folds and select M0"]
      C4 --> C5["validate_m0_tuning()\nexpand or accept valid null/cap"]
      C5 --> C6["fit_m0() on all T_H\nfreeze_m0()"]
    end

    C6 --> D
    subgraph M1["M1: alignment — nested LOSO"]
      D["For each fold F in T_H"] --> D1["Rebuild fold-local M0\nusing T_H minus F"]
      D1 --> D2["Fit/tune M1 on T_H minus F"]
      D2 --> D3["Walk forward and score alignment on F"]
      D3 --> D4["Record peak/phase loss and boundaries"]
      D4 --> D
      D4 --> D5["Aggregate all folds and select M1"]
      D5 --> D6["validate_m1_tuning()\nexpand or accept valid null/cap"]
      D6 --> D7["fit_m1() using frozen all-T_H M0\nfreeze_m1()"]
    end

    D7 --> E
    subgraph M2["M2: forecast — nested full LOSO"]
      E["For each fold F in T_H"] --> E1["Use fold-local M0 and M1\nwith F still unseen"]
      E1 --> E2["Build fold M1 walk-forward\ncompact handoff cache"]
      E2 --> E3["Fit/evaluate every M2 candidate\non T_H minus F; score F"]
      E3 --> E4["Record NLL, horizon/phase loss, boundaries"]
      E4 --> E
      E4 --> E5["Aggregate all folds and select M2"]
      E5 --> E6["validate_m2_tuning()\nexpand or accept valid null/cap"]
      E6 --> E7["fit_m2() using frozen M0/M1\nfreeze_m2()"]
    end

    E7 --> F["assemble_kit()\nvalidate_page_kit()"]
    A -. "H is untouched until here" .-> G["Replay H sequentially\nreplay_season_holdout(..., kit_compatibility='strict')"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["Audit predictions, metrics, provenance,\nand add one comparable table row"]

    classDef holdout fill:#fff2cc,stroke:#b8860b,color:#000;
    classDef gate fill:#e8f1f8,stroke:#1e5f8e,color:#000;
    class A,G,H holdout;
    class B,C5,D6,E6,F gate;
```

## What “full LOSO” means at each stage

| Stage | Fold-local fitting data | Fold evaluation | Final fit after the gate | Main leakage protection |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M0 ignition** | `T_H \ {F}` | Detect ignition prospectively on `F`; compare with its declared label | Fit the selected M0 configuration on all `T_H` | No detector threshold is selected using `F` or `H` |
| **M1 alignment** | Fold-local M0 is rebuilt on `T_H \ {F}`; M1 reference/templates use that same fold data | Walk alignment forward on `F`; score peak, phase, and alignment errors | Fit selected M1 with the frozen all-`T_H` M0 | A global M0 reference is never reused as if it were fold-independent |
| **M2 forecast** | Fold-local M0/M1 states and M1 walk-forward predictions; M2 fit uses `T_H \ {F}` | Forecast horizons 1 and 2 on `F`; score Bernoulli NLL and diagnostics | Fit selected M2 with frozen all-`T_H` M0/M1 | `manual_labels_train` excludes `F`; held-out labels are not supplied to the fold |

The M1 and M2 rows are deliberately nested. Passing one global M0 or M1
artifact through every fold would make the downstream score optimistic. The
complete M1 phase cache is retained for audit/resume, while
`compact_m1_cache_for_m2()` sends only the handoff needed by M2 workers.

## Stage gates and expansion decisions

Each stage has four distinct states:

```text
tune_* -> validate_*_tuning(check_boundaries = TRUE)
       -> fit_* -> freeze_*
```

The next stage cannot start from a draft or from a tuning object alone:

1. M0 must have complete finite LOSO folds and a valid selected configuration.
2. M1 requires a frozen M0 with the exact same `page_season_selection` and
   matching data identity.
3. M2 requires the exact frozen M0/M1 identity chain and complete fold scores.
4. `assemble_kit()` requires all three frozen stages and rechecks provenance.

A non-null winner at a tested grid edge is not silently accepted. Inspect it
with `inspect_tuning_boundaries()`, append one controlled adjacent value with
`expand_tuning_grid()`, and rerun the same folds. A value at an edge may stop
only when it is an explicit null/drop choice, a valid structural cap, or when
the predeclared minimum-gain rule justifies stopping. Expansion must finish
before the holdout is viewed.

## Canonical manual call sequence

The following is a template; supply the authorized data and the grids for the
cycle. It intentionally shows the low-level calls so that every gate is
visible. `train_pipeline(mode = "retune")` composes the same lifecycle when a
single orchestrator is preferred.

```{r}
# H is the only season reserved for replay.
holdout <- "2024-25"
permanent_exclusions <- c("2011-12", "2020-21", "2021-22")
eligible <- setdiff(sort(unique(allD$season)), permanent_exclusions)
training <- setdiff(eligible, holdout)

selection <- validate_season_selection(
  allD,
  training_seasons = training,
  exclude_seasons = permanent_exclusions,
  holdout_seasons = holdout,
  application_seasons = character()
)

# M0: complete LOSO, validate, fit and freeze.
m0_tuning <- tune_m0(allD, selection = selection, grid = m0_grid)
m0_tuning <- validate_m0_tuning(m0_tuning, check_boundaries = TRUE)
m0 <- fit_m0(allD, selection, config = m0_tuning$best_params) |>
  freeze_m0(tuning = m0_tuning)

# M1: fold-local M0/M1 LOSO is performed by the governed tuner.
m1_tuning <- tune_m1(
  allD, selection = selection, m0 = m0,
  grid = m1_grid, checkpoint_dir = "checkpoints/m1"
)
m1_tuning <- validate_m1_tuning(m1_tuning, check_boundaries = TRUE)
m1_best <- m1_tuning$best[1, , drop = FALSE]
m1_config <- m1_make_params(
  k_ref = m1_best$k_ref,
  temperature = m1_best$multi_temperature,
  rise_weight = m1_best$align_rise_weight,
  slope_window = m1_best$slope_window,
  slope_weight = m1_best$slope_weight
)
m1 <- fit_m1(allD, selection, m0, config = m1_config) |>
  freeze_m1(tuning = m1_tuning)

# M2: fold-local M0/M1 predictions, complete candidate evaluation, then freeze.
m2_tuning <- tune_m2(
  allD, selection, m0, m1, grid = m2_grid,
  checkpoint_dir = "checkpoints/m2"
)
m2_tuning <- validate_m2_tuning(m2_tuning, check_boundaries = TRUE)
m2 <- fit_m2(allD, selection, m0, m1, config = m2_tuning$best_spec) |>
  freeze_m2(tuning = m2_tuning)

kit <- assemble_kit(m0, m1, m2)
validate_page_kit(kit)

# Only now is H opened.
replay <- replay_season_holdout(
  kit, allD, season = holdout, kit_compatibility = "strict"
)
```

For a boundary expansion, keep the same selection, checkpoint directory, and
fold definitions. Pass the previous tuning result to the expansion helper so
completed specification IDs are reused; do not restart a fresh grid that loses
the prior audit trail.

## What is and is not comparable

Rows marked **exchangeable** use the same season-selection and governed
stage-order rules. Same-holdout variants are useful for implementation checks
(for example, the two 2018–19 expanded retries), but they are not additional
independent seasons. The 2015–16 drop-test and historical legacy variants must
remain labelled as special evidence. Cross-season metric ranking is descriptive
because seasons differ in difficulty; promotion decisions require a
predeclared candidate/incumbent comparison on the same untouched holdout.

## Evidence to retain for every cycle

Each season directory should retain, at minimum:

- the normalized season selection and data identity;
- M0, M1, and M2 tuning results, grids, fold scores, and boundary reports;
- frozen `m0`, `m1`, and `m2` artifacts plus the assembled kit;
- checkpoint directories needed to resume additive expansion;
- the strict replay object, predictions, aggregate metrics, and warnings; and
- a run manifest recording package version, API mode, host, cores, and paths.

The holdout replay is the final evaluation artifact, not an input to another
search. Any tuning change after viewing it starts a new pre-holdout cycle.
